# Intake Brief: help screen and improved help line (WL-0MTV97GV20088CS7)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work-item selection list footer advertises only a small, mixed-signal
subset of the available keyboard shortcuts — including the low-value
`d:downtime toggle` and the mouse-tracking hint `alt+m mouse on` — while offering
no discoverable reference for the full command set or for the meaning of the
icons rendered on each row. Users cannot discover what keys are available or
what the glyphs mean without reading the source.

## Users

Herdr producers and agents who navigate work items in the pane-based selection
list and rely on the footer and on-screen glyphs to operate the tool.

**User stories:**

- As a Herdr user, I want a single `?` shortcut that opens a help screen, so I
  can discover every available command without reading the source.
- As a Herdr user, I want the help screen to explain every icon shown in the
  list, so I can interpret the status, stage, priority, risk, effort, audit and
  agent glyphs at a glance.
- As a Herdr user, I want the footer help line to advertise the help screen
  rather than rarely-used toggles, so the most useful discovery path is always
  visible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Footer help line updated** — In the selection list footer, the
   `d:downtime toggle` entry is no longer advertised and `?: Help` is shown
   instead. The `d` key binding itself remains functional (only its inline
   advertisement is removed).
2. **Mouse hint removed from footer** — The `alt+m mouse on` / `alt+m mouse off`
   footer hint is removed. The `Alt+m` mouse-tracking toggle itself remains
   functional and is documented in the help screen.
3. **Help screen opens on `?`** — Pressing `?` in the selection list opens a
   dedicated help screen (full-pane overlay). Pressing `?`, `Esc`, or `q`
   dismisses it and returns to the list with no state mutation (selection,
   filters, and navigation stack unchanged).
4. **Help screen lists all commands** — The help screen enumerates every
   registered shortcut available in the selection list, grouped by chord
   leader, showing the chord key(s), label and a short description. The list is
   derived from the live `ShortcutRegistry` so future shortcut additions appear
   automatically.
5. **Help screen identifies all icons** — The help screen includes an icon
   legend that identifies every glyph rendered in work-item rows (at minimum:
   status, stage, priority, epic, risk, effort, audit, producer-review, agent
   state and child-coverage icons), each with a short meaning.
6. **Graceful on small panes** — The help screen renders within the pane height
   without overflowing the `rows - 1` render budget (scroll or truncate when
   content exceeds the viewport; the dismiss keys remain discoverable).
7. **Tests** — New/updated tests verify: (a) the footer shows `?: Help` and no
   longer shows `d:downtime toggle` or `alt+m mouse on/off`; (b) the help
   screen renders the registered commands and the icon legend; (c) `?` toggles
   the help screen on and off without mutating list state.
8. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, `docs/TUI.md`, the icon legend in
   `docs/icons-design.md` (if the on-screen legend wording is authoritative) and
   any relevant README entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not break existing chord handling: `?` must not conflict with any
  registered shortcut chord or navigation key.
- Backward compatibility: all existing shortcut key bindings (including `d` and
  `Alt+m`) continue to function unchanged; only their footer advertisement
  changes.
- The help screen is display-only/read-only — it must not dispatch commands, spawn
  panes, or mutate the worklog.
- Icon legend content must be derived from the single source of truth
  (`@worklog/shared/icons`) rather than a hand-maintained duplicate list, so it
  cannot drift.
- Must respect the existing `showHelpText` gate (when help text is disabled, the
  help screen and its footer hint are not offered).

## Existing state

- **Footer hint assembly** — `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` composes the
  footer from `formatFooterShortcutHints()` (single-key entries render as
  `key:label`) plus an explicit mouse-tracking hint appended at render time
  (`dynamicHints` around the "Mouse-tracking toggle hint
  (WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN)" block). The `d` entry comes from
  `src/shortcuts.json` (`chord: ["d"]`, `label: "downtime toggle"`).
- **View modes** — `ViewMode = 'list' | 'detail' | 'filter' | 'form'`
  (`worklist.ts`). `renderWorklist()` branches on mode; `filter` mode shows a
  simple full-pane prompt — the closest existing precedent for a full-pane help
  overlay.
- **Key handling** — `keyToAction()` maps navigation keys; single-key shortcut
  resolution and chord handling happen in the main key loop. No `?` handling
  exists today.
- **Icons** — all row glyphs come from `@worklog/shared/icons`
  (`statusIcon`, `stageIcon`, `priorityIcon`, `epicIcon`, `riskIcon`,
  `effortIcon`, `auditIcon`, `needsProducerReviewIcon`, `agentStatusIcon`,
  `getIconPrefixParts`/`isCoveredByParent`). `docs/icons-design.md` documents the
  icon set and accessible labels.
- **Shortcut registry** — `ShortcutRegistry.getChordEntries()` /
  `getEntriesForStage()` expose all valid entries with `chord`, `label` and
  `description`, gated by code-freeze and issue-type.

## Desired change

1. **Footer (`formatFooterShortcutHints` / render-time composition):**
   - Exclude the `d:downtime toggle` single-key entry from the footer hint (or
     suppress its advertisement while keeping the binding).
   - Prepend/insert a literal `?: Help` hint.
   - Remove the `alt+m mouse on/off` suffix block.

2. **New help mode:** add `'help'` to `ViewMode`; render a full-pane help
   overlay in `renderWorklist()` with two sections — **Commands** (grouped by
   leader, `chord → label — description`) and **Icons** (glyph → meaning) —
   respecting the pane height budget.

3. **Key binding:** in list mode, `?` toggles the help mode on; inside help
   mode, `?`, `Esc` and `q` return to the previous mode (record the
   pre-help mode, mirroring the existing `preFormMode` pattern).

4. **Tests:** extend `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or a focused
   `worklist-help.test.ts`) for the footer and help-screen behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `ViewMode`, `formatFooterShortcutHints()`,
  footer composition (mouse-hint block), `renderWorklist()` help overlay, key
  handling (`?`), help-content builder.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcut-config.ts` — `ShortcutRegistry` used to enumerate
  commands for the help screen (read-only; no signature change expected).
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — icon definitions used to build the legend
  (read-only; source of truth).
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — shortcut definitions; no new entry
  required if `?` is a reserved key, but a `?` entry may be added for
  discoverability.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (and/or new
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist-help.test.ts`) — footer and help-screen tests.
- `docs/TUI.md` — document the `?` help screen and updated footer.
- `docs/icons-design.md` — icon legend reference (update if wording is
  authoritative).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — shortcut/help summary if present.

## Related work

- **WL-0MQDR5HZC006JWOK** — "Show available shortcut keys in browse list help
  text" (completed). Introduced the dynamic shortcut hint line this work
  extends.
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** — "help line for chord commands too verbose"
  (completed). Collapsed/trimmed chord hints in the same footer.
- **WL-0MQDUOK9K002QHJU** — "Stage-based shortcut condition filters" (completed).
  Added stage-aware shortcut filtering used when enumerating help entries.
- **WL-0MT0AP2LR000JFWN** — mouse-tracking toggle (`Alt+m`) whose footer hint
  this work removes.
- **WL-0MSZ4NSOE007AQEF** — `/downtime toggle` command backing the `d` shortcut.
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** — "Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the
  selection list" (completed). Directly related: owns the mouse-tracking
  behaviour whose `Alt+m` footer hint this work removes.
- **WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94** — heading/display-row model used by the renderer.
- **WL-0MTV979LK005YB1B** — footer wrap guard (relevant to keeping the help
  overlay within the render budget).

None of these are duplicates or blockers — they provide historical context for
the footer, chord and renderer subsystems.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MTD0IVNN003WCOB** – Warn in wl export/import --help that export dumps the whole DB and import REPLACEs it (completed)
- **WL-0MUN4ARHA001SN40** – Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old (open)
- **WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ** – Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, alt, commands, downtime, help (+13 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, alt, downtime, help, icons (+10 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — `d` binding retained:** "replace `d:downtime toggle` with
  `?: Help`" is interpreted as replacing the footer *advertisement* only; the
  `d` key continues to toggle downtime and is documented in the help screen.
- **Assumption — `Alt+m` retained:** the mouse-tracking toggle remains
  functional; only its footer advertisement is removed (documented in the help
  screen).
- **Assumption — list view scope:** the help screen is offered in the selection
  list. Detail-view command help is out of scope unless trivially reachable.
- **Risk — key conflict:** `?` must not collide with a registered chord or
  navigation key; verify against `shortcuts.json` and `keyToAction()`.
- **Risk — icon-legend drift:** hard-coding the legend duplicates the icon
  source of truth. Mitigate by deriving rows from `@worklog/shared/icons` where
  practical, or add a test asserting every legend glyph matches the exported
  icon.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a full command *reference* (rendering help text for
  detail/form modes) is out of scope; record such follow-ups as linked work
  items rather than expanding this one.
- **Small-pane risk:** the combined commands + icons content can exceed short
  panes; require truncation/scroll so the footer stays one row and the render
  invariant holds.
- **Performance risk:** negligible — help content is computed only when the
  help screen is opened.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were asked — the work-item description and code analysis
provided sufficient detail. Assumptions above were applied where the seed
context was ambiguous and are recorded for producer review.

# Intake Brief: CTRL-r manual refresh shortcut + remove `[auto-refresh on]` header indicator

## Problem statement

The Herdr worklist selection list can only refresh via the event-driven watcher / 30 s auto-refresh tick; there is no reliable manual-refresh key. The legacy `r` refresh was removed (commit `6b98e67b`, WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA) because `r` is now a chord leader (Producer Review / Interview), leaving the `refresh` action in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` unreachable from list mode. Separately, the header always shows a `[auto-refresh on]` message while `autoRefresh` is enabled — visual noise that the user wants gone.

## Users

- **Operator / TUI user of the herdr worklist selection list** — wants an immediate, unambiguous "refresh now" key so edited items appear without waiting for the auto-refresh cycle, and wants a cleaner header.

User stories:
- As a worklist user, when I press `Ctrl+r`, the selection list immediately re-fetches items from the worklog DB and re-renders, preserving my selection when the item still exists.
- As a worklist user, I want the header to stop showing `[auto-refresh on]` so the header stays short and conveys only count/filter/status.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Pressing `Ctrl+r` (`\x12`) while the worklist is in **list mode** immediately triggers the existing refresh path (`doRefresh(true)`): items are re-fetched from the DB, the list re-renders, and the currently selected item stays selected when it still exists in the refreshed list. Covered by a `handleKeypress` unit test (`keyToAction('\x12') === 'refresh'`).
2. `Ctrl+r` does **not** conflict with the `r` chord leader: bare `r` continues to start the Producer Review / Interview chords (`r p`, `r i`) exactly as today, and no chord/shortcut changes are made to `shortcuts.json`.
3. The `[auto-refresh on]` segment is **never rendered** in the header, regardless of the `autoRefresh` setting. Header rendering keeps the count / filter / `(top N of M)` / `[paused — hidden]` / downtime segments. The renderer test that currently asserts `[auto-refresh on]` (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` ~L5915) is updated to assert its absence, and header-fit tests still pass.
4. `Ctrl+r` remains functional when `autoRefresh` is disabled (the setting still controls the scheduler tick; the shortcut is independent of it).
5. Manual refresh is documented: `packages/herdr/README.md` gains a `Ctrl+r` entry in the navigation/keybindings section, and any stale references to "manual `r`" refresh (README ~L266 "Manual `r` always runs", `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` ~L38) are updated to `Ctrl+r`.
6. **Testing/validation criterion:** full `packages/herdr` unit suite (`worklist*.test.ts`) passes with the changes.
7. **Documentation criterion:** all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (README keybindings + stale `r` refresh references; the worklist renderer comment noting the parameter's retained-for-compatibility status).
8. **Suite criterion:** full project test suite (`npm test` → vitest) passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The legacy `r` refresh must NOT be restored (it conflicts with the `r` chord leader — WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA); `Ctrl+r` is the new binding.
- Do not change `shortcuts.json`; the `r` chords, `S` Ship It, and all other bindings stay as-is.
- No change to the auto-refresh *schedule* or DB-change gating — only the header message is removed and a manual refresh shortcut is added.
- The `refresh` action already exists end-to-end (`keyToAction` → `handleKeypress` `case 'refresh'` → `handleKeyInput` `if (action === 'refresh') → doRefresh(true)`); the change just re-instates a reachable key for it.
- Keyboard scope: list mode only (the user asked for the *selection list*; the detail view keeps its current behaviour). KeypressDecoder already emits a lone control char (`\x12`) as its own token, so no decoder change is needed.
- Live keyboard blink: `\x12` is not a herdr prefix/leader and is not bound elsewhere; no conflicts known.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`:
  - `keyToAction()` (L~2852) maps navigation keys; the `r → refresh` case was removed by commit `6b98e67b` (WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA). The `case 'refresh'` in `handleKeypress` (L~3073) and `if (action === 'refresh') { await doRefresh(true); }` (L~6385) are still present but unreachable in list mode.
  - Renderer `createListRenderer` (L~3835) header block (L~3966-3968): `if (autoRefresh) { header += ' ${ANSI.dim}[auto-refresh on]${ANSI.reset}'; }`. `autoRefresh` is passed positionally from the single production call site (`opts.autoRefresh`, L~6618) and by many tests.
  - `doRefresh(true)` (L~5511) already preserves selection across refreshes (item matched by ID).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — L~5915 asserts header contains `[auto-refresh on]`; several header-fit tests pass `autoRefresh` positionally.
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — `r`-chord-leader tests at ~L542-554.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — §2 navigation list (no refresh entry); L~266 "Manual `r` always runs"; L~1422/1592 "manual actions never gated".
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` L~38 — "`r`/`S`-style refreshes".

## Desired change

1. **Bind `Ctrl+r`.** In `keyToAction()` add `case '\x12': return 'refresh';` (Ctrl+R is byte 0x12). Because `\x12` is not a chord leader and not a single-key shortcut, the existing `action === 'refresh'` branch fires `doRefresh(true)` — the immediate, selection-preserving refresh. No changes to `shortcuts.json`, the chord registry, or the decoder.
2. **Remove the header indicator.** Delete the `if (autoRefresh) { header += ' [auto-refresh on]'; }` block in the renderer. Keep the `autoRefresh` parameter (positional callers across the codebase/tests depend on it) but mark it intentionally unused with a comment, OR cleanly remove it if the implementer verifies no positional caller shifts break. Recommended: keep the parameter with a documented "retained for positional call-site compatibility" comment (surgical, no test churn beyond the indicator assertions).
3. Update the header tests to assert the indicator is absent, add a `keyToAction('\x12')`/`handleKeypress` Ctrl+r test, and add a README keybinding entry + fix stale `r` references.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `keyToAction` (\x12 → 'refresh'), renderer header block removal, parameter compatibility comment.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — header-indicator test update (L~5915), new Ctrl+r mapping test, header-fit test hygiene.
- `tests/herdr/worklist.test.ts` — verify/add Ctrl+r coverage alongside the `r`-chord-leader tests (L~542).
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — §2 keybinding list + L~266 manual-refresh wording.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — L~38 "`r`/`S`-style refreshes" → `Ctrl+r`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "selection list view" = the Herdr worklist pane (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) — its header is the only place `[auto-refresh on]` renders. The Pi TUI browse widget has no such header and is out of scope (confirmed by searching both `packages/herdr` and `packages/tui`).
- **Assumption (based on the explicit "use CTRL-r" directive):** the binding is `Ctrl+r` (byte `\x12`) and replaces any notion of bare-`r` refresh, which remains reserved for the review/interview chords.
- **Risk — dead parameter:** left unused, `autoRefresh` in the renderer becomes dead weight; mitigation = documented compatibility comment (or clean removal if the implementer verifies positional callers).
- **Risk — stale docs:** README `Manual `r`` claims (L~266, L~1422/1592) and `pause-when-hidden.md` already reference a removed `r` refresh; update them with the CTRL-r wording so documentation doesn't point at a non-existent key.
- **Scope-creep risk:** removing the `[paused — hidden]` indicator, changing the auto-refresh interval, or re-adding bare-`r` refresh are all out of scope; anything discovered during implementation should be recorded as a linked work item, not absorbed here.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA** (completed) — removed the legacy `r → refresh` mapping ("fix(herdr): remove legacy r->refresh mapping in list mode", commit `6b98e67b`); rationale this change must not reverse.
- **WL-0MTA217DZ003H5K8** (completed) — shortcut commands (close/delete/update) now refresh the selection list immediately; same `doRefresh` path.
- **WL-0MQJL1W3X0055WJH** (completed) — 5 s auto-refresh for the *Pi TUI* browse selection list (different widget, useful context).
- **WL-0MSBVCMNO00503QM** (completed) — staleness indicator in the selection list when its refresh is paused (related header/footer rendering area).
- **WL-0MS31X52O0061C79** (completed) — auto-refresh & auto-sync implementation that introduced the `[auto-refresh on]` header segment (`ac76444a`).
- **WL-0MSJ1OLTL009N4IQ** (completed) — DB-change gated auto-refresh with "Manual `r` always runs" wording.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should `Ctrl+r` also refresh while in the detail view, or just the selection list?" — Not asked: the seed explicitly scopes to the **selection list view**; list-mode-only is the reasonable default and is recorded as an assumption (AC 1). If the producer wants detail-view refresh too, AC 1 can be widened.
- Q2: "Should the auto-refresh *schedule* change (interval/DB-gate) or only the header message?" — Not asked: the seed says "Remove the message", not the feature; the setting remains functional (AC 4).
- Q3: No clarifying questions required — seed context was unambiguous and all other details were resolved by repo research (header location, existing refresh action, chord conflict, docs references). Any deviation the producer wants (e.g. detail-mode scope) is a small AC amendment.

## Effort and risk (preliminary)

- **Effort:** Small (XS–S) — a one-line key mapping, a 3-line header deletion, test updates and doc wording. No new modules or settings.
- **Risk:** Low — touches a well-covered unit surface (`keyToAction`, header renderer); no lifecycle/status/DB semantics; the main care points are not resurrecting bare-`r` and keeping positional renderer callers intact.

## RM summary (research)

Confirmed the legacy `r → refresh` mapping was removed in commit `6b98e67b` (WL-0MS4LDWHW0062FTA) leaving the `refresh` action dead in list mode; confirmed the `[auto-refresh on]` header segment is unique to the Herdr worklist renderer (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` L~3967, introduced by `ac76444a`/WL-0MS31X52O0061C79) and appears in only one test assertion (L~5915); confirmed `KeypressDecoder`/`splitKeypresses` passes lone control characters through unchanged so `\x12` arrives as a single token; confirmed `\x12` is not a chord leader and no shortcut binds it, so the existing `action === 'refresh' → doRefresh(true)` handler is reachable with no registry changes; surveyed docs for stale `r` refresh references (README L~266, `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` L~38). No completed or open item duplicates this work (existing items cover Pi-TUI browse auto-refresh and post-command refresh, not a Ctrl+r binding or header cleanup).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKRSO1KD1NWWYBP** – Persist Worklog DB across executions; refresh from JSONL when newer (completed)
- **WL-0MQK8EBNT002XMR7** – wl list --parent <id> does not include childCount in JSON output (completed)
- **WL-0MKRPG5ZD1DHKPCV** – Feature: Automation ergonomics (sort/limit/fields/bulk) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, auto, ctrl, header, herdr, immediately, indicator, keyboard, list, manual, refresh, remove, selection, shortcut, view, worklist
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: add, auto, header, herdr, immediately, indicator, keyboard, list, refresh, remove, selection, shortcut, view, worklist
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, auto, header, herdr, immediately, indicator, list, manual, refresh, remove, selection, shortcut, view, worklist
data.title: Add CTRL-r manual refresh shortcut and remove auto-refresh header indicator from the worklist selection list

# Test-first: assignee-CAS claim and status-neutral audit-dispatch contract

Author the failing tests that pin the contract for child C2 (`wl update --if-assignee`) and child C4 (status-neutral audit-tier claim). This item is deliberately created **before** the implementation items (test-first ordering).

## Goal (user story)

As an agent, I want executable tests that define the exact assignee-CAS and status-neutral claim behaviour, so the implementation is driven by a failing-first contract and regressions in the claim path are caught immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit tests exist for `wl update --if-assignee <value>`: exact-match success, mismatch is a no-op/stale result with no partial write, `--if-assignee ""` succeeds when the current assignee is empty, and `--if-assignee ""` fails when the assignee is non-empty.
- [ ] Atomicity test: two concurrent `--if-assignee ""` claims against the same item yield exactly one winner (single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction).
- [ ] Integration test: a `completed`/`in_review` item claimed by the audit tier reads back as `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` — never an `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid.
- [ ] Regression test: a simulated audit Phase-2 failure after a herdr claim restores `completed`/`in_review` and the item is re-selectable by the audit tier.
- [ ] Failing-first evidence recorded (tests red before C2/C4 land, green after); no implementation code is written in this item.

## Constraints

- Tests only — no production code changes in this work item.
- Use the existing test layout (`tests/unit/`, `tests/cli/`, `packages/shared/src/*.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/*.test.ts`).
- Must not depend on the `needsProducerReview` column.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` — extend the existing `updateIfMatches()` CAS suite
- `tests/cli/` — `wl update --if-assignee` CLI integration tests
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts` — dispatch/claim integration tests
- `tests/unit/` — sync regression-guard fixtures (shared with C3)

## Deliverables

Failing-first test files plus a comment recording the red/green evidence.

# Add `wl update --if-assignee` atomic CAS

## Goal (user story)

As an agent competing for a work item, I want an atomic assignee compare-and-swap guard on `wl update`, so a status-neutral claim can have exactly one winner without changing the item's status or stage.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `wl update <id> --assignee <v> --if-assignee <expected>` applies only when the current assignee matches `expected`; on mismatch it returns a stale/no-op result and writes nothing.
- [ ] The guard runs in a single `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction through the `updateIfMatches` CAS primitive (the expected-match surface is extended to `assignee`).
- [ ] `--if-assignee ""` is a meaningful expected value (matches an empty assignee) and is distinguishable from the flag being omitted.
- [ ] `--if-assignee` composes with `--if-status`/`--if-stage` in one atomic guard; existing `--if-status`/`--if-stage` behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] The C1 unit + CLI integration tests pass; `CLI.md` documents the new flag.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `updateIfMatches`/`UpdateWorkItemInput` expected-match typing to include `assignee` (`packages/shared/src/database.ts`, `src/persistent-store.ts`, `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts`).
- Add `--if-assignee <assignee>` to the update command and wire it into the existing CAS branch (`src/commands/update.ts`: option, `normalizeActionArgs`, `hasProvided` normalisation, `updateIfMatches` call, stale-result message).
- Normalise the empty string as an explicit expected value (mirroring the assignee normalisation used for writes).

## Constraints

- Atomicity and single-winner semantics must match the existing `--if-status`/`--if-stage` claim (RCA WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT design point 1).
- Do not change other commands' CAS surface.

## Key Files

# Assignee sync regression-guard decision and implementation

## Goal (user story)

As an operator syncing across roots, I want a decided, documented and tested rule for how `assignee` merges, so a cleared assignee (releasing a scheduling hold) propagates cross-root instead of being refused as a regression and resurrecting stale claims.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Epic open question Q1 is answered and recorded with rationale: (a) treat `assignee` as a normal non-regression-guarded merge field so `''` clears propagate, or (b) keep it regression-guarded and document the cross-root rule. **Recommended: (a).**
- [ ] If (a): `assignee` is removed from the regression-guard merge-participating paths (`src/sync.ts` around the `mergeParticipatingFields` definitions) and a cross-root test proves a remote `''` clears a local non-empty assignee **without** `--accept-regressions`.
- [ ] If (b): the cross-root rule is documented and a test covers the `--accept-regressions` path plus the refused-clear behaviour.
- [ ] A cross-root sync test (two worklog roots) exercises the chosen rule end-to-end.
- [ ] No other merge field's regression behaviour changes.

## Constraints

- Must not weaken regression protection for `status`, `stage` or `priority`.
- The decision must be recorded in the parent epic Appendix as the accepted answer.

## Key Files

- `src/sync.ts`
- `tests/unit/` (sync regression-guard fixtures)
- `docs/dev/` (cross-root sync notes)

## Deliverables

`src/sync.ts` change (or documented decision), tests, docs.

# Status-neutral audit-tier claim and guarded rollback (herdr)

## Goal (user story)

As an operator running herdr downtime dispatch, I want the audit-tier claim to change only the assignee, so an audited `completed`/`in_review` item never enters a hybrid state and a failed audit can never strand it off the review queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `claimWorkItem` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) issues `wl update <id> --assignee <agent> --if-status completed --if-stage in_review --if-assignee ""` — it writes no `--status` and no `--stage`.
- [ ] The item reads back as `completed`/`in_review` via `wl show` throughout the claim (no `in-progress`/`in_review` hybrid).
- [ ] `rollbackClaimWorkItem` clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`, so only this claim's state is reverted.
- [ ] Exactly-one-winner is preserved (the C1 concurrency test passes).
- [ ] `classifyItemForDispatch`/the audit-tier `select*` functions exclude items with a non-empty assignee, so assigning an item to the producer makes the claim fail stale at every tier.
- [ ] Tests cover: claim keeps completed/in_review; concurrent claim single-winner; an assignee-held item is not dispatched.

## Constraints

- **No hybrid status/stage write**: the new claim path must never produce `in-progress`/`in_review`.
- The `--if-assignee ""` guard is the exclusive token; rollback is guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>`.
- Cross-root claim targeting keeps the existing `--worklog-dir` convention.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (`claimWorkItem`, `rollbackClaimWorkItem`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`classifyItemForDispatch`, `select*`, `dispatchClaimedTier`)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`

## Deliverables

Status-neutral claim, guarded rollback, assignee-based selection exclusion, tests.

# Failed-dispatch recovery clears the assignee

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want every dispatch failure path to release the claim's assignee, so a marker-write-failed or spawn-failed dispatch never strands an item as permanently unclaimable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The marker-write-failed recovery path clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>` and leaves the item re-selectable.
- [ ] The spawn-failed recovery path clears the assignee guarded by `--if-assignee <agent>` and leaves the item re-selectable.
- [ ] After each failure mode, `wl show` shows `completed`/`in_review` with an empty assignee.
- [ ] Tests cover both failure modes and assert re-selectability by the audit tier.
- [ ] No dispatch failure mode can leave a non-empty assignee behind.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`rollbackClaimForFailure`, recovery/stranding paths)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker*.test.ts`

## Deliverables

Recovery-path change plus tests.

# Assignee-hold scheduling convention and producer sentinel

## Goal (user story)

As a producer, I want an explicit per-item way to pause automatic scheduling — by assigning the item to myself — that does not rely on a magic DB flag, with a well-known sentinel value the release gate can recognise.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Epic open question Q2 is answered and recorded: the literal producer-hold value is a reserved, well-known value equal to the producer's wl identity (self-describing, reusable by the release gate). **Recommended:** reserved identity value, exact literal confirmed with the producer.
- [ ] The convention is documented: a non-empty assignee means "intentionally held from auto-dispatch"; assigning to the producer is the per-item pause switch.
- [ ] Every ContextHub/SorraAgents assignee writer is audited (intake, plan, implement, triage, delegate `@github-copilot`, `status_lifecycle`) and clears the assignee on session end; `status_lifecycle`'s failure-exit already clears it.
- [ ] A test proves that clearing a claim's assignee makes the item dispatchable again (hold released).
- [ ] Correctness risk R1 is addressed by the clearing-discipline audit (no writer silently suppresses auto-dispatch).

## Constraints

- The sentinel must not collide with real agent identities.
- Must not strand in-flight implement/plan/intake claims: only session-end clearing is added.

## Key Files

- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents)
- `AGENTS.md` (draft claim/hold pattern; finalised in C12)

## Deliverables

Sentinel decision, convention documentation, clearing-discipline changes, test.

# Audit runner: clear assignee on terminal verdicts and preserve completed/in_review on failure

## Cross-repo note

This work item is implemented in the **SorraAgents** repo (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`); a SorraAgents (SA) work item is created there and linked from this epic. AGENTS.md forbids editing `skill/` dirs without explicit instruction.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the audit runner to release its assignee claim on every terminal outcome and never coerce a review-queue item out of `completed`/`in_review` on failure, so auto-dispatched audits leave no residue and re-runs still dispatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On the success ('yes') verdict path the runner clears the assignee (`--assignee ""`), retains `completed`/`in_review`, and applies the producer hold required by policy.
- [ ] On the failure-restore path the runner restores `completed`/`in_review` and clears the assignee — the inlined `_STATUS_STAGE_COMPAT` coercion of `in_review → plan_complete` is no longer reachable for review-queue items.
- [ ] The SIGKILL abort-recovery (state-file) path restores `completed`/`in_review` and clears the assignee.
- [ ] On the 'no' verdict path the runner clears the assignee.
- [ ] Unit + integration tests cover each terminal path, including the captured-pre-audit-state = status-neutral-claim case.
- [ ] A SorraAgents work item exists for this change and is linked as related work.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (SorraAgents)
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (SorraAgents)

## Deliverables

audit_runner.py changes, tests, linked SA work item.

# One-time legacy assignee residue cleanup

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the existing assignee residue cleaned up once, idempotently and narrowly, so the review queue drains instead of ossifying under 700+ stale producer holds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An idempotent script clears assignee residue on the ~698 completed + ~7 in_review audit-hold items only; it never clears in-flight implement/plan/intake claims.
- [ ] A dry-run mode prints the affected items and counts before any write.
- [ ] Re-running the script is a no-op (no further writes reported).
- [ ] The script is tested against a fixture database covering: audit-hold residue (cleared), in-flight claim (untouched), and already-clean items (untouched).
- [ ] Ordering is documented: the script runs **after** the code change ships (status-neutral claim + assignee-based selection, C4/C6).

## Constraints

- Idempotent; scoped to audit-hold residue; never touches `needsProducerReview` (removed separately).
- Must not run until C4/C6 have shipped (documented in the work item).

## Key Files

- `scripts/` (new cleanup script)
- `tests/` (fixture-DB tests)

Cleanup script, dry-run mode, tests.
